So, there exist\ sequences $\varepsilon_k\to 0$, $R_k=\varepsilon_k^{-1}$, $\mathsf{h}_k,\Sigma^k, \hat{\mathtt{g}}^k , \mathtt{g}^k, \varphi_k, \mathsf{f}_k, \psi_k$ such that\ the assumptions (i)--(iii) in Proposition \ref{p.lin.ac} are satisfied for \((\varepsilon, R, \mathsf{h}, \Sigma, \hat{\mathtt{g}}, \mathtt{g} ) = ( \varepsilon_k, R_k, \mathsf{h}_k, \Sigma^k, \hat{\mathtt{g}}^k, \mathtt{g}^k )\), \eqref{e.lin.AC} is satisfied for \((\varphi, \mathsf{f}, \psi ) = (\varphi_k, \mathsf{f}_k, \psi_k )\), and 
\begin{equation}\label{e.norm.1,0}
	\|\varphi\|_{C^{0}_{\sigma}\left(\Sigma^k_{(-2\delta R)}\times \mathbb{R}\right)} =1, \left(\|\psi\|_{C^{1,\theta}_{\sigma}\left(\partial_0\Sigma_{(-\delta R)}\times \mathbb{R}\right)} + \|\mathsf{f}\|_{C^{0,\theta}_{\sigma}\left(\Sigma_{(-\delta R)}\times \mathbb{R}\right)}\right) \to 0.
\end{equation} 
Hence\ there exists\ $(p_k,s_k)\in \Sigma^k_{(-2\delta R)}\times \mathbb{R}$ and $c>0$ such that\ 
\begin{equation}\label{e.(p_k,s_k)}
	e^{\sigma s_k}|\varphi(p_k,s_k)|\geq c.
\end{equation}

If $q\in \text{int}(\Sigma^k_{(-2\delta R)})$, using a normal coordinate system (cf. Lemmas \ref{l.exp.map}, \ref{l.tilde.t.Pi}) of \(\Sigma^k\) centreed at \(q\), we can find $Y_q:\mathbb{B}_r(0)\to \text{int}(\Sigma_k)$, where $r=\min\{R_k^{1/2}, d(q,\partial\Sigma^k), \delta R_k\}$, such that\ $Y_q$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image, $Y_q(0)=q$, $\|(Y_q^*\mathtt{g}^k)_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\|_{C^2} = o(1)$ uniformly as $k\to \infty$. Similarly, if $q\in \partial \Sigma^k_{(-2\delta R)}$, using a Fermi coordinate system (cf. Lemmas \ref{l.Fermi.coord}, \ref{l.exp.map}, \ref{l.tilde.t.Pi}) of \(\partial \Sigma^k\) centreed at \(q\), we can find $Y_q:\mathbb{B}^+_r(0)\to \Sigma_k$, where $r=\min\{R_k^{1/2}, \delta R_k\}$, such that\ $Y_q$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image, $Y_q(0)=q$, $\|(Y_q^*\mathtt{g}^k)_{ij}-\delta_{ij}\|_{C^2} = o(1)$ uniformly as $k\to \infty$.

Let $(p_k,s_k)$ be as in \eqref{e.(p_k,s_k)}. There are three possibilities:
\begin{equation}\label{e.p_k.del.Si^k}
	\text{(i)}\;\limsup_{k\to \infty} d(p_k,\partial \Sigma^k) = \infty,\;\text{(ii)}\; \limsup_{k\to \infty} d(p_k,\partial_0 \Sigma^k) < \infty,\; \text{(iii)}\; \limsup_{k\to \infty} d(p_k,\partial_+ \Sigma^k) < \infty.
\end{equation}
If (i) happens, we set $q_k=p_k$; if (ii) (resp. (iii)) happens, we set $q_k$ to be the nearest point in \(\partial_0 \Sigma^k\) (resp. \(\partial_+ \Sigma^k\)) to $p_k$. Suppose\ $\limsup_{k\to \infty} |s_k| <\infty$. Then in all the three cases (in \eqref{e.p_k.del.Si^k}), we define $Y_k = Y_{q_k}$, $\tilde{\varphi}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= \varphi_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)$, \(\tilde{\mathsf{f}}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= \mathsf{f}_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)\), and in case (ii) $\tilde{\psi}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= \psi_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)$. Then \(\tilde{\varphi}_k\) satisfies the following equation.

\begin{equation}\label{e.tilde.vp.k.eq}
	-a^{ij}_k\partial_{\mathtt{y}_i\mathtt{y}_j} \tilde{\varphi}_k - b^i_k \partial_{\mathtt{y}_i} \tilde{\varphi}_k - \partial_{ss} \tilde{\varphi}_k + W''(\mathbb{H})\tilde{\varphi}_k = \tilde{\mathsf{f}}_k,
\end{equation}
where \(\|a^{ij}_k-\delta_{ij}\|_{C^{0,\theta}} + \|b^i_k\|_{C^{0,\theta}}=o(1)\) as \(k\to \infty\). In case (i), \eqref{e.tilde.vp.k.eq} is satisfied on \(\mathbb{B}_{r_k}(0) \times \mathbb{R} \), where \(r_k=\min\{R_k^{1/2}, d(q_k,\partial\Sigma^k), \delta R_k\}\). Therefore\ by \eqref{e.norm.1,0}, there exists\ a bounded function\ \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R})\) such that\ up to a subsequence, \(\tilde{\varphi}_k \to \tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\) in \(C^2_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R})\),
\[-\Delta_{\mathtt{y}} \tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} - \partial_{ss}\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} + W''(\mathbb{H})\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} =0 \text{ on }\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R},\]
and \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}(\mathtt{y},s)\mathbb{H}'(s)ds=0\) for all\ \(\mathtt{y}\in \mathbb{R}^n\). Hence\ by Lemma \ref{l.entire.lin.ac}, \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\equiv 0\). However, this is a contradiction since \eqref{e.(p_k,s_k)} implies there exists\ $s_{\infty}\in \mathbb{R}$ such that\ \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}(0,s_{\infty}) \neq 0\). In case (ii) (resp. (iii)), \eqref{e.tilde.vp.k.eq} is satisfied on \(\mathbb{B}^+_{r_k}(0) \times \mathbb{R} \), where \(r_k=\min\{R_k^{1/2}, \delta R_k\}\) and $\partial_{\nu} \tilde{\varphi}_k=\tilde{\psi}_k$ (resp. \(\tilde{\varphi}_k = 0 \)) on \(\partial_0\mathbb{B}^+_{r_k}(0) \times \mathbb{R} \). Therefore\ by \eqref{e.norm.1,0}, there exists\ a bounded function\ \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n_+ \times \mathbb{R})\) such that\ up to a subsequence, \(\tilde{\varphi}_k \to \tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\) in \(C^2_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n_+ \times \mathbb{R})\),
\[-\Delta_{\mathtt{y}} \tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} - \partial_{ss}\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} + W''(\mathbb{H})\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} =0 \text{ on }\mathbb{R}^n_+ \times \mathbb{R},\]
\(\partial_{\nu}\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} = 0 \) (resp. $\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} = 0$) on \(\partial \mathbb{R}^n_+ \times \mathbb{R} \)  and \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}(\mathtt{y},s)\mathbb{H}'(s)ds=0\) for all\ \(\mathtt{y}\in \mathbb{R}^n_+\). Hence\ by Lemma \ref{l.entire.lin.ac}, \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty}\equiv 0\). However, this is a contradiction since \eqref{e.(p_k,s_k)} implies there exists\ $s_{\infty}\in \mathbb{R}$ such that\ \(\tilde{\varphi}_{\infty} (0,s_{\infty}) \neq 0\). 

If $\limsup_{k\to \infty} |s_k| =\infty$, without loss of generality we can assume that \(s_k \to \infty\) as \(k\to \infty\). Let us consider the three possibilities stated in \eqref{e.p_k.del.Si^k} and define \(q_k\) as above. In all the three cases (in \eqref{e.p_k.del.Si^k}), we define $Y_k = Y_{q_k}$, $\tilde{\varphi}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= e^{\sigma (s_k + s)}\varphi_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)$, \(\tilde{\mathsf{f}}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= e^{\sigma (s_k + s)}\mathsf{f}_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)\), and in case (ii) $\tilde{\psi}_k(\mathtt{y},s)= e^{\sigma (s_k + s)} \psi_k(Y_k(\mathtt{y}), s)$. Then \(\tilde{\varphi}_k\) satisfies the following equation.

\begin{equation}\label{e.tilde.vp.k.eq'}
	-a^{ij}_k\partial_{\mathtt{y}_i\mathtt{y}_j} \tilde{\varphi}_k - b^i_k \partial_{\mathtt{y}_i} \tilde{\varphi}_k - \partial_{ss} \tilde{\varphi}_k + 2\sigma \partial_s \tilde{\varphi}_k + (W''(\mathbb{H}(s_k+s)) - \sigma^2)\tilde{\varphi}_k = \tilde{\mathsf{f}}_k,
\end{equation}
where \(\|a^{ij}_k-\delta_{ij}\|_{C^{0,\theta}} + \|b^i_k\|_{C^{0,\theta}}=o(1)\) as \(k\to \infty\). Arguing as in the previous case and using Lemma \ref{l.entire.lin.ac'}, we again arrive at a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- lemma-53: body_md -->
\label{global gluing estimates 1}
	Let us fix $\delta_i>0$, $i=0,1,2,3$, satisfying $\delta_0+\delta_1+\delta_2<\delta_3$ and $a,b>0$. Let $r\in (0, \delta_1R)$, $\rho\in(1,\delta_2R)$, $p\in B^+_{\delta_0R}(0)$, $B^{+}_{s}(p)=B_s(p)\cap B^+_{2R}(0)$, $U\in C^{2,\theta}(B^+_{\delta_3R}(0))$ with the uniform estimates
\begin{equation}\label{e.U.bound}
	U\geq a>0, \quad U+|\nabla U|\leq b \text{ on }B^+_{\delta_3R}(0).
\end{equation}
Then there exists\ a constant $C>0$ independent of $r,\: \rho,\: p,\: U,\: \varepsilon$ with\ the following significance.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item If $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small\footnote{The metric\ $g$ in \eqref{e.De-1} depends on $\varepsilon$.} and $\varphi\in C^2(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))$ satisfies
	\begin{equation}\label{e.De-1}
		\begin{cases}
			\Delta_g\varphi-U\varphi=E+\operatorname{div}(F)\text{ on } B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p),\\
			\partial_\nu \varphi=\psi \text{ on }\partial_0 B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p),\\
		\end{cases}
	\end{equation}
	there holds
	\begin{equation}\label{e.est1.De-1}
		\left|\varphi\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r}(p))}\leq C\left(\left|E\right|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+\left|F\right|_{C^\theta(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))} +\left|\psi\right|_{C^{0, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+\rho^{-1}\left|\varphi\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\right).
	\end{equation}	

\item If $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small and $\varphi\in C^2(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{e.De-1'}
	\begin{cases}
		\Delta_g\varphi-U\varphi=E+\operatorname{div}(F)\text{ on } B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p),\\
		\varphi=\psi \text{ on }\partial_0 B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p),\\
	\end{cases}
\end{equation}
there holds
\begin{equation}\label{e.est1.De-1'}
	\left|\varphi\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r}(p))}\leq C\left(\left|E\right|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+\left|F\right|_{C^\theta(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))} +\left|\psi\right|_{C^{1, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+\rho^{-1}\left|\varphi\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\right).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-53 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
The proof is similar to \cite[proof of Lemma 8.1]{del2016introduction}. Since the proofs of (i) and (ii) are very similar, we will prove only (i). Let us first prove the following claim.
	\begin{claim}\label{outer claim1}
	There exists\ a constant $C>0$ independent of $r,\: \rho,\: p,\: U,\: \varepsilon$ such that\ if	$\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $\tilde{\varphi},\tilde{E},\tilde{F},\tilde{\psi}$ are compactly supported in $B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p)$ and \eqref{e.De-1} is satisfied for $(\varphi,E, F, \psi) =(\tilde{\varphi},\tilde{E},\tilde{F},\tilde{\psi})$, there holds 
		\begin{equation}\label{e.est2.De-1}
			|\tilde{\varphi}|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\leq C\left(|\tilde{E}|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{F}|_{C^\theta(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{\psi}|_{C^{0, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\right).
		\end{equation}
	\end{claim}
 To prove this claim, we assume by contradiction that the estimate \eqref{e.est2.De-1} does not hold. Then there exist\ sequences $\tilde{U}_i, \tilde{\varphi}_i,\tilde{E}_i,\tilde{F}_i,\tilde{\psi}_i$, $r_i,\: \rho_i,\: p_i,\: \varepsilon_i$ such that\  $\varepsilon_i\rightarrow 0$, $\tilde{\varphi}_i,\tilde{E}_i,\tilde{F}_i,\tilde{\psi}_i$ are compactly supported in $B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i)$, 
		\begin{equation}\label{e.est.tph_n}
			|\tilde{\varphi}_i|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i))}=1,\quad \left(|\tilde{E}_i|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i))}+|\tilde{F}_i|_{C^\theta (B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i))} +|\tilde{\psi}_i|_{C^{0, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i))}\right)\rightarrow 0
		\end{equation} 
		and \eqref{e.De-1} is satisfied for $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_i$ and 
		$$(U,\varphi,E, F, \psi,r,\rho,p)=(\tilde{U}_i, \tilde{\varphi}_i,\tilde{E}_i, \tilde{F}_i, \tilde{\psi}_i,r_i, \rho_i, p_i).$$
Then
	\begin{align}\label{phi_n-equation out}
			& \hat{g}^{jk}(\varepsilon_i\cdot)\partial_{jk}\tilde{\varphi}_i-\varepsilon_i\hat{g}^{jk}(\varepsilon_i\cdot)\hat{\Gamma}_{jk}^l(\varepsilon_i\cdot)\partial_{l}\tilde{\varphi}_i-\tilde{U}_i\tilde{\varphi}_i=\tilde{E}_i+\operatorname{div}\tilde{F}_i \text{ on } B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i);\\
			&\partial_{\nu}\tilde{\varphi}_i=\tilde{\psi}_i\text{ on }\partial_0 B^{+}_{r_i+\rho_i}(p_i).
	\end{align}
Since $\tilde{\varphi}_i,\tilde{E}_i,\tilde{F}_i,\tilde{\psi}_i$ are compactly supported, we can assume that \eqref{phi_n-equation out} holds on $B^+_{\delta_3 R}(0)$. Let $\delta'_3=\delta_0+\delta_1+ \delta_2$. There exists\ $\tilde{x}_i\in B^+_{\delta'_3 R}(0)$ such that\ $|\tilde{\varphi}(\tilde{x}_i)|\geq 1/2$. 

Suppose $\limsup_{i\to\infty} \tilde{x}_{i,1} =\infty$. We define $\bar{\varphi}_i(x)=\tilde{\varphi}_i(\tilde{x}_i+x)$. Then $|\bar{\varphi}_i(0)|\geq 1/2$ and (by Theorem \ref{t.sch}) the $C^{1,\theta}$ norm of $\bar{\varphi}_i$ is uniformly bounded on $B(0,s_i)$ where $$s_i=\frac{1}{2}\min\left\{\tilde{x}_{i,1},(\delta_3-\delta'_3)R_i\right\}.$$
Therefore\ there exist\ $\varphi_{\infty},U_{\infty}:\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that\ up to a subsequence, $\bar{\varphi}_i \to \varphi_{\infty}$ in $C^1_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$,  
\[\Delta_{g_E}\varphi_{\infty}-U_{\infty}\varphi_{\infty}=0 \text{ on }\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\]
and $|\varphi_{\infty}(0)|\geq 1/2$. However, this contradicts Lemma \ref{l.entire.lin.ac'}(i).

On the other hand, if $\limsup_{i\to\infty} \tilde{x}_{i,1} <\infty$, we define $\bar{x}_i=(0,\tilde{x}_{i,2},\dots, \tilde{x}_{i,n+1})$ and $\bar{\varphi}_i(x) =\tilde{\varphi}_i(\bar{x}_i+x)$. The $C^{1,\theta}$ norm of $\bar{\varphi}_i$ is uniformly bounded on $B(0,\frac{1}{2}(\delta_3-\delta'_3)R_i)$. Therefore\ there exist\ $\varphi_{\infty},U_{\infty}:\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
\begin{align}
	& \Delta_{g_E}\varphi_{\infty}-U_{\infty}\varphi_{\infty}=0 \text{ on }\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+,\\
	& \partial_{\nu}\varphi_{\infty}=0 \text{ on }\partial\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+.
\end{align}
Moreover, $|\varphi_{\infty}(x_{\infty})|\geq 1/2$ for some $x_{\infty}\in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+$, which contradicts Lemma \ref{l.entire.lin.ac'}(iii). This finishes the proof of the claim. 
	
	To prove the lemma, we choose a cut-off function $0\leq\chi\leq1$ such that\ $\chi=1$ on $B^+_r(p)$, $\text{spt}(\chi)\subset B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p)$, $\left|\nabla \chi\right|+\left|\nabla^2 \chi\right|\lesssim \rho^{-1}$ and apply the above claim to $\tilde{\varphi}=\chi\varphi$. Indeed, $		\Delta_{g}\tilde{\varphi} -U\tilde{\varphi} =\tilde{E}+\textrm{div}(\tilde{F}) \text{ on } B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p)$, where $\tilde{E}=\chi E+2\langle\nabla \varphi, \nabla \chi\rangle +\varphi\Delta\chi-\langle F, \nabla \chi\rangle $, $\tilde{F}=\chi F$ and $\partial_{\nu} \tilde{\varphi}=\tilde{\psi}\quad \text{on }\partial_0 B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p)$ where $\tilde{\psi}=\chi\psi+\varphi\partial_1\chi$. Therefore, the lemma follows from above claim and  elliptic estimate
	\begin{align}
		\left|\varphi\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r}(p))}&=\left|\tilde{\varphi}\right|_{C^{1,\theta}(B^{+}_{r}(p))}
           
		  
        \lesssim \left(|\tilde{E}|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{F}|_{C^\theta(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{\psi}|_{C^{0, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+\left|\tilde{\varphi}\right|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\right).    
	\end{align}
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- claim-8: body_md -->
\label{outer claim1}
	There exists\ a constant $C>0$ independent of $r,\: \rho,\: p,\: U,\: \varepsilon$ such that\ if	$\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $\tilde{\varphi},\tilde{E},\tilde{F},\tilde{\psi}$ are compactly supported in $B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p)$ and \eqref{e.De-1} is satisfied for $(\varphi,E, F, \psi) =(\tilde{\varphi},\tilde{E},\tilde{F},\tilde{\psi})$, there holds 
		\begin{equation}\label{e.est2.De-1}
			|\tilde{\varphi}|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\leq C\left(|\tilde{E}|_{C^{0}(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{F}|_{C^\theta(B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}+|\tilde{\psi}|_{C^{0, \theta}(\partial_0B^{+}_{r+\rho}(p))}\right).
		\end{equation}
<!-- end claim-8 -->
